example: In `src/lib.rs`, a method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`; a method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`; and a method `read` declared in `trait Read` has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
rationale:
The example `requirements.references.selector_impl_and_trait` gives a concrete case in `src/lib.rs`. A method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`. A method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`. A method `read` in a trait has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`.

Both referenced tests build Rust source with an inherent `impl Thing { fn run() {} }`, a trait impl `impl Trait for Thing { fn run() {} }`, and `trait Trait { fn read(&self); }`.

- `src/…/outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` parses the source as `src/lib.rs`. It asserts that the selector set contains `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]` and `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`. It also checks that each selector resolves to a node whose stored selector equals it.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates]` asserts the same three selectors, using the file name `lib.rs`.

The tests name the trait `Trait` instead of `Read`. The example only illustrates the `trait[Name]/fn[method]` form, so this does not matter. The same tests cover the inherent-impl and trait-impl cases, so a selector that mixed up the two would be caught.

The example cites `requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`. Both tests also cover that requirement's impl-segment naming, `impl[Thing]` versus `impl[Thing/Trait]`, as it applies to this case.

I did not read the `outline` and `selectors` helpers. I judged them only by how the tests use them.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
